lxc_3bea9b3e81a791c3.text: In the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland, people wear costumes.

lxc_afa8913953e3f8de.text: A costume is clothing that makes someone look like another person or thing, such as a witch or a ghost.

lxc_e19b993abba343db.text: Children go from door to door.

lxc_6d48bcf7e2212717.text: At each door, they say “Trick or treat!”

lxc_fd2aa439a1633aa7.text: Children often carry a bag for their candy.

lxc_c9bb5b29a1252893.text: A parent or another adult often walks with young children.

lxc_fbe954058a889e3a.text: Some Halloween costumes are scary, and some are funny.

lxc_753682fcac34db28.text: One person can dress as a ghost, and a friend can dress as a big banana.

lxc_8e356eefb8f38d97.text: Many go to costume parties, where people meet friends in their costumes.

lxc_c12567ca0d9d2f18.text: People also cut pumpkins into jack-o-lanterns.

lxc_360c62c725bf52ae.text: They take out the inside of a pumpkin and cut a face into it.

lxc_e4104dd443bc76bb.text: A light inside the pumpkin makes the face shine in the dark.

lxc_7fbe7104f7e836ff.text: Canadian Thanksgiving is the second Monday of October.

lxc_ffcf259abf66be0a.text: 1 October is a Thursday, so 5 October is the first Monday and 12 October is the second Monday.

lxc_1e1f167d49472776.text: Families sit down for a harvest meal, often on the Sunday or the Monday.

lxc_cba6f086fbd88697.text: Roast turkey is a common main dish.

lxc_d926b14b46618bc8.text: Families often serve it with stuffing, potatoes, and cranberry sauce.

lxc_ee750dc13cfd0706.text: Stuffing is a mixture often made with bread.

lxc_1a3df5a0fed2202c.text: Pumpkin pie comes after the main meal.

lxc_d371c0ff6ec1ce57.text: People give thanks for the harvest and the year.

lxc_d53bcf5ce85187f2.text: Since 1957, Canadian Thanksgiving has been on the second Monday of October.

lxc_6675c9b8834b23df.text: In 2026, the long weekend runs from Saturday 10 October to Monday 12 October.

lxc_4908e16e1fa83b26.text: A long weekend gives many people three days away from school or work.

lxc_fcb77435cf41197b.text: Many people travel home to see family and share the harvest meal.

lxc_c1ffce703594857f.text: Thanksgiving is a day off in most of Canada, so schools, banks, and many workplaces close.

lxc_70bcaa9636d030f6.text: In French, the day is called Action de grâce.

lxc_cb96a747f0833773.text: People often say “Happy Thanksgiving” to family and friends.

lxc_aad101ff7a9579b1.text: People in the United States keep Thanksgiving on the fourth Thursday of November.

lxc_0ac624eefad22fce.text: German Unity Day is on 3 October.

lxc_0a8869cb12f7c111.text: Its German name is Tag der Deutschen Einheit.

lxc_931e5f2b36572a6a.text: Germany was once East Germany and West Germany.

lxc_5f54cf5eae842c68.text: Their official names were the German Democratic Republic and the Federal Republic of Germany.

lxc_473a7cbf447d1b9a.text: The Berlin Wall divided East and West Berlin.

lxc_d3589ff685324fa0.text: After protests, the Berlin Wall opened on 9 November 1989.

lxc_3b5fa01292b0c8db.text: On 3 October 1990, East Germany joined West Germany.

lxc_02c6e9ca8c12d915.text: German Unity Day is a public holiday, so people have the day off.

lxc_bdcb4c1cfb47d9f8.text: Each year, one German state hosts the main celebration.

lxc_501f8d2a9e0795bb.text: Its city-centre festival runs from 2 to 4 October, and it is free to enter.

lxc_c3f65f115ad9d3e2.text: People can hear concerts and talks across the city centre.

lxc_7522352505ea34fa.text: Berlin also has events near the Brandenburg Gate, a famous landmark in the city.

lxc_156f981777123f4a.text: People see black, red, and gold flags and hear speeches about the country and its history.

lxc_fa28e8ec4ec4b040.text: October has three special days in this lesson: Halloween on 31 October, Canadian Thanksgiving on 12 October, and German Unity Day on 3 October.
